// Purpose (see Spec Section 2 / 9): establishes the Mongoose connection using MONGODB_URI
// from the environment. Mongoose is the ODM used for schema validation and transactions.
// Fail fast on bad queries and keep buffering behaviour predictable in tests.
* Connect to MongoDB using the MONGODB_URI env var.
* Returns the active mongoose connection so callers can await readiness.
throw new Error('MONGODB_URI is not set — see .env.example (Spec Section 9).');
// Surface connection-level errors that happen after the initial connect.
// redis.js — Shared Redis connection (ioredis) used as the broker/storage layer for BullMQ.
// Purpose (see Spec Section 7.6): creates one shared ioredis connection from REDIS_URL so both
// job producers (jobs/) and consumers (workers/) reuse the same connection. Redis is used ONLY
// as the BullMQ broker, not as the primary database.
// BullMQ requires maxRetriesPerRequest: null on the connection it uses for blocking commands.
// Export the single shared connection so jobs/ and workers/ don't each open their own.
// User.js — Mongoose model for application users (admin/staff) who log in and manage BillFlow.
email: { type: String, required: true, unique: true, lowercase: true, trim: true },
// Never store raw passwords — only the bcrypt hash (Spec Section 7.3 / 8).
// Customer.js — Mongoose model for customers that businesses bill and track balances for.
//   billingAddress Object { line1, city, state, zip, country }
// Sub-document for the billing address — no separate _id needed.
name: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
email: { type: String, required: true, lowercase: true, trim: true },
balance: { type: Number, default: 0 }, // running outstanding balance
// Invoice.js — Mongoose model for invoices (manual + recurring) issued to customers.
// Line item sub-document — an invoice can have multiple products/services.
total: { type: Number }, // = quantity * unitPrice, calculated at creation time
// Human-readable ID shown to customers (e.g. "INV-2026-0042"). Auto-generated at creation.
customerId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Customer', required: true },
subtotal: { type: Number }, // sum of all item totals, before tax
totalAmount: { type: Number }, // subtotal + tax — final amount owed
// Only relevant when isRecurring is true; null otherwise.
pdfUrl: { type: String }, // filled in after PDFKit runs
// "sparse" so the unique constraint only applies to docs that actually set it.
// The real idempotency check happens via the IdempotencyKey collection (Spec Section 7.1).
idempotencyKey: { type: String, unique: true, sparse: true },
// Payment.js — Mongoose model for payments recorded against invoices.
invoiceId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Invoice', required: true },
// Denormalized so we don't always need to look up the invoice just to know who paid.
customerId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Customer', required: true },
transactionRef: { type: String }, // external reference from payment gateway (if any)
// "sparse" — unique only for docs that set it. See Spec Section 7.1.
idempotencyKey: { type: String, unique: true, sparse: true },
// Spec 5.4 lists only createdAt (no updatedAt) for Payment.
// AuditLog.js — Mongoose model capturing before/after state of sensitive domain operations for compliance.
// Note (Spec 7.3): never log passwords or payment card data in beforeState/afterState.
action: { type: String, required: true }, // e.g. 'INVOICE_CREATED', 'PAYMENT_UPDATED'
// Mixed — captures an arbitrary snapshot of the entity before/after the change.
// IdempotencyKey.js — Mongoose model storing idempotency keys + cached responses to prevent duplicate writes.
// This collection stores ONLY idempotency keys and their cached responses — no business data.
// Import Mongoose — the ODM (Object Document Mapper) we use to talk to MongoDB
// Schema definition for the IdempotencyKey collection
// The unique key sent by the client in the "Idempotency-Key" request header.
// "unique: true" means MongoDB itself will reject a duplicate insert of the same key.
key: { type: String, required: true, unique: true },
// The HTTP status code returned the first time this request was processed (e.g. 201).
// The actual response body sent back the first time. "Mixed" so it can hold any shape.
// "expires: 86400" creates a TTL index — MongoDB deletes this doc 24h after createdAt.
// Idempotency keys only protect against short-term retries, not long-term storage.
createdAt: { type: Date, default: Date.now, expires: 86400 },
// Export the compiled model so the middleware can import and use it.
// idempotency.middleware.js — Express middleware that short-circuits duplicate POSTs using the Idempotency-Key header.
// Purpose (see Spec Section 7.1): checks the IdempotencyKey collection for the request's
// "Idempotency-Key" header; if found, returns the previously stored response without re-running
// the controller; if new, lets the request proceed and caches the key + response afterward.
// This is an Express middleware — it runs BEFORE the actual controller function.
// (req, res, next) is the standard Express middleware signature.
// Read the "Idempotency-Key" header (Express lowercases header names).
// No key → skip protection and let the request go through normally.
// Has this exact key been used before?
// Already processed — return the SAME response we sent the first time,
// without re-running the controller (no duplicate invoice/payment).
// --- New request we haven't seen before ---
// Keep a reference to the real res.json so we can call it after caching.
// Override res.json: when the controller calls res.json(body), first persist the
// key + response, THEN send the response to the client.
key, // the same key from the header
statusCode: res.statusCode, // whatever status the controller set (e.g. 201)
response: body, // the actual response data the controller is sending
return originalJson(body); // now actually send the response
// Continue to the actual controller (e.g. createInvoice).
// Export so routes can plug this in before their controller functions.

description: Claude Code sandbox here blocks outbound network and socket bind — affects npm native builds and running the backend server
The Claude Code security sandbox on this machine blocks (1) outbound network to
nodejs.org, github.com, and even registry.npmjs.org (raw curl → HTTP 403 "Domain
blocked"), and (2) binding a listening socket (`app.listen`/supertest → `listen EPERM`).
**Why:** Environment security constraints, not code defects. Discovered while scaffolding
- `npm install` fails on the `bcrypt` native addon: no prebuilt binary for Node 24, and
the source build can't fetch Node headers (nodejs.org blocked) or the prebuilt binary
(github.com blocked). The toolchain (clang 16, python3) IS present — it's purely network.
Workarounds: run install via Bash with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`, add the domains
`npm install --ignore-scripts` succeeds and proves the dependency tree resolves.
- Can't HTTP-smoke-test a server here (socket bind denied). Verify boot instead by
`require()`-ing the app and walking `app._router.stack`; models via `mongoose.modelNames()`.
- The machine's default `node` is v14.17.6 (below the backend's `engines: >=20`). Use nvm:
- [Sandbox network & bind restrictions](sandbox-network-and-bind-restrictions.md) — why `npm install` (bcrypt) and running the server fail here; use nvm Node 24 + `--ignore-scripts`.
